conventions: In the ASV's 'accuse X of Y' frame for κατηγορέω, the English 'of' belongs to the token realizing the thing accused of, never to the genitive of the person and never to the verb: MRK.15.3 gives 'of many things' to πολλά and a bare 'him' to αὐτοῦ, and MRK.15.4 gives the clause-final 'of' to πόσα discontinuously under rule 15 and a bare 'thee' to σου. Stranding the preposition at the end of the English clause does not move it, rules 53 and 63 having already refused to read a helper off English word order.

A supplied English preposition that the ASV's verb idiom requires, where no Greek preposition is expressed and no Greek case answers to it, is a rule 7 helper on the verb that licenses it: 'clothe … with' at 15.17 (double accusative, no preposition), 'asked of him' at 15.6, 'calling unto him' at 15.44, 'part … among them' at 15.24. Where the English preposition realizes an expressed Greek case it rides with its own noun or pronoun instead, under rules 21 and 23's determinerless clause: 'with a reed' at 15.19 and 'with a … voice' at 15.34 (instrumental dative), 'of vinegar' at 15.36, 'of God' at 15.39. A supplied lexical verb is not such a helper: it is 'added' under rule 5 together with its own complement, as 'to go with them' is at 15.21, where ἀγγαρεύω's complement stands nowhere in the projection, and as the repeated 'to do' is at 15.8 under rule 103.

Rule 34's pleonastic reading of ἀπὸ μακρόθεν is scoped to the ASV's 'afar off', where no English word answers to the preposition separately. Where the ASV instead writes 'from afar', as at 15.40, the 'from' answers to ἀπό and rule 2 splits the pair, the ASV's phrasing deciding as it does for an improper preposition under rule 42's closing clause. The competing reading is named in that unit's note.
report: One real cross-verse split, at MRK.15.3 / MRK.15.4: the English 'of' of the ASV's 'accuse X of Y' frame. Both verses render κατηγορέω with a genitive of the person and an accusative of the thing, but 15.3 gives 'of many things' to πολλά and a bare 'him' to αὐτοῦ, while 15.4 gave the clause-final 'of' to σου ('thee of') as though it realized the genitive. It does not: 15.3 writes 'accused him', not 'accused of him'. Nothing in the source licenses the difference, only the ASV's stranding of 'of' at the clause end, and rules 53 and 63 have already refused to read a helper off English word order. Patched 15.4 only: πόσα now takes the discontinuous 'how many things … of' under rule 15, headed on 'many' as before, and σου takes a bare 'thee'. 15.3 is left as it stands, being the chapter norm and matching every other complement 'of' here (of vinegar, of God, of James, of Joses).

Articles: every difference is source-licensed. Rule 23 before a name is unanimous across sixteen verses; rule 20's displacement (15.19 τὴν κεφαλήν, 15.20, 15.21, 15.24, 15.26, 15.29, 15.34) is held apart from rule 20's second arm at 15.19 τὰ γόνατα -> 'their', where no genitive pronoun stands; rule 31 empties the second attributive article at 15.39 because κεντυρίων is expressed, while rule 32 splits the substantival ones at 15.2, 15.7, 15.29, 15.32, 15.35 and rule 90's closing clause splits 15.41; rule 57 keeps 'the' on the article across an interposed name at 15.22 and interposed genitives at 15.40; and 15.47's 'the mother' on the article against 15.40's bare 'the' differs because μήτηρ is expressed at 15.40 and supplied at 15.47 (rule 102).

Other groups checked and found context-licensed: ἵνα as 'to' (15.15, 15.20) and as 'that' (15.11, 15.21, 15.32) is one analysis under rules 40 and 24; negation divides correctly between rule 41 (15.4 Οὐκ empty, 'nothing' on οὐδέν), rule 69 (15.5 'anything' is non-negative, so 'no more' stays on οὐκέτι), rule 39 (15.31 οὐ δύναται -> 'cannot') and an ordinary 'not' at 15.23; supplied 'when' sits on a participle in all six instances (rule 86); the rule-88 juncture sits on the verb it introduces in all seven (15.1 twice, 15.8, 15.12, 15.36, 15.37, 15.43, 15.46); ἐκπνέω heads on 'ghost' at both 15.37 and 15.39; rule 73 is applied both ways in one chapter, collapsing ἱκανὸν ποιῆσαι -> 'to content' at 15.15 and splitting συμβούλιον ποιήσαντες -> 'held' / 'a consultation' at 15.1.

Read the dump end to end for the split the candidate table is blind to — a supplied word marked 'added' in one verse and folded in another. The two 'added' units are both supplied lexical verbs: 'to go with them' at 15.21, licensed by no source token, and the repeated 'to do' at 15.8, whose ποιέω is already spent on 'do' (rule 103). Everything folded elsewhere is either a function word (15.6 'of him', 15.17 'with', 15.24 'among them', 15.44 'unto him', 15.31 'him', 15.7 'lying', 15.40 'were') or the source word's own English expression (15.7 'men', 15.42 'the day before the sabbath', 15.43 'estate', 15.47 'mother'). Repeated English folds onto its one source token where it is a pronoun (15.27 'his his', 15.46 'him him') and is 'added' where it is lexical (15.8), which is rule 103's own division. No split.

BSB: both disagreements are documented convention differences and neither is an error. 15.4 Οὐκ is rule 41's redundant negative before οὐδέν -> 'nothing', which rule 41 says in terms is not a correction; 15.21 τὸν is τὸν σταυρὸν αὐτοῦ, emptied by rule 20's displacement. No accepted edge was touched to move the rate, and the patch above changes only target edges, not represented/unrepresented status, so the comparable set is unaffected.

Noted but not changed: 15.40 ἀπὸ μακρόθεν -> 'from afar' aligns ἀπό to 'from' rather than leaving it unrepresented. Rule 34 is scoped to the rendering 'afar off', where English realizes the preposition nowhere; the ASV wrote a separate 'from' here, so rule 2 splits the pair, exactly as rule 42's closing clause lets the ASV's phrasing decide an improper preposition. The unit note names the competing reading and I have recorded the scoping in the conventions log. No promotion: the corpus packet carries no μακρόθεν rows, and a qualification of rule 34 written without them would be a rule the corpus might contradict.
